To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the discourse in collaborative learning can be readily characterized as networks of arguments and counter arguments, and the quantitative measures of the argument structures are positively related to improvement of the students' ability on a learning task.
the discourse structure of peer discussions is a mediator of learning and that the quality of the argumentation structure is positively related to improvement of writing skills.

the structure of peer discussions about writing conclusions is a network of arguments about the quality of the conclusions and that the complexity of that structure is positively related to improvement on a writing task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the peer interaction that occurs in a collaborative learning environment and the ways in the structure of that interaction affects what students learn.
the structure of peer learning.
the role that peer discourse plays in the development of scientific reasoning and writing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of peer learning discourse is a significant mediator of learning in collaborative learning situations.
peer learning is an effective way to learn.
peer learning is effective when the discourse structure is argumentative and complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of peer interactions matters.
the structure of discourse is a mediator of learning in peer learning.
students learn more when they discuss the merits of their ideas and when they are required to defend their positions than when they simply discuss whether their ideas are OK or not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of students' peer interactions is a function of the structure of the discourse.
the structure of peer learning discourse is important.
it is important for teachers to consider how they structure the peer interactions in their classroom to support the development of argumentative discourse.
